description: Chaos testing, network emulation, and stress testing tool for containers

summary.one_liner: Pumba is a chaos testing and network emulation CLI for Docker, containerd, and Podman containers that can kill, stop, pause, or remove containers, inject network faults, and stress container resources.
summary.what_it_does: Pumba is a Go command-line tool for injecting faults into running containers. It can kill, stop, pause, remove, or restart containers, and run commands inside them via exec. Its netem subcommands add egress latency, packet loss, duplication, corruption, and rate limits, and can combine several effects in one qdisc. The iptables subcommand drops packets, including ingress. The stress subcommand applies CPU, memory, and I/O load through stress-ng. Targets can be chosen by name, regex (re2:), label, or at random, and actions can recur on an interval. A status command finds leftover iptables rules, qdiscs, and sidecars from a crashed run, and ndjson output is available for scripts.
use_cases: Test how a service behaves when its container is killed or restarted
Simulate network latency or packet loss between containers
Verify application resilience under CPU or memory pressure
Run recurring random chaos experiments against a staging cluster
Inject faults into containers from CI pipelines
Clean up leftover network faults after an interrupted chaos run
how_to_run: curl -sL -o pumba (download the release binary for your platform), then chmod +x pumba
notable: Supports Docker, containerd, and Podman through one CLI, with runtime-specific notes on socket paths and namespaces
netem combine applies delay, loss, and other effects in a single owned qdisc
Result events in ndjson format plus a status --check command that reports leftover faults and exits 0 only when clean
Includes --dry-run, --max-targets safety cap, and --max-duration time budget
Runs as a Docker image built natively for amd64 and arm64
caveats: Linux only: Windows is explicitly unsupported and not planned; macOS is for driving remote VMs, and Podman on macOS requires running pumba inside podman machine
netem, iptables, and stress need root or rootful Podman; containerd needs root for sidecar mounts
Network chaos needs tc or iptables in the target container, or a --tc-image sidecar
Docker Hub image is deprecated; ghcr.io is the primary registry
